verified.hardware: nvidia_grace_blackwell (Dell Pro Max GB300, GB300 only; RTX PRO 2000 display GPU not used)
verified.smoke: tool call (get_weather) ok; single stream decode p50 188.7 tok/s, TTFT p90 1.0 s
notes: Measured with the kit's agent concurrency bench (coder/solstice method, doc-check reviews), launched as an llm-helper profile with this image and these flags; the recipes launch path itself was not run on the GB300.
Interactive limit (p90 TTFT <= 10 s, p10 decode >= 15 tok/s): 4 reviews, 6.2 concurrent chats, 4.2 concurrent calls.
Autonomous plateau: 16 reviews, 3060.0 turns/hour; users chatting ~20.0.

Profile as benched (after 3 failed starts): glm53-flash-arm64-cu130, 0.92, --max-num-seqs 480 (Mamba blocks), --max-cudagraph-capture-size 128, no --tokenizer-mode. Kit profile's --max-num-seqs 4 would have capped it at 4 concurrent calls.

What set the limits: decode speed per stream and KV cache, not errors (0 errors, 0 timeouts at every step). Prefix-cache hit is ~0.47 at every step (Nemotron 0.81-0.93), so each turn re-reads ~half its prompt; KV cache (2.87 M tokens at 0.92) reached 93% max at only ~20 concurrent calls (N 16) and saturated at N 32, where turns/hour fell 3060 -> 1620 and TTFT p90 jumped to 44 s. The GPU drew ~1,190 W of its 1,300 W limit already at N 16. MTP x3 helps single-stream decode (189 tok/s) but the advantage is gone by N 16 (p50 25 tok/s).
